Chicken and courgette rice porridge
50 g skinless chicken breast
Cut the chicken into small pieces and dice the courgette and carrot; wash the rice.
Put the chicken and water in a pan, bring to the boil and skim off the foam.
Add the rice and carrot and cook over low heat for 15 minutes.
Add the courgette and cook for 10 more minutes, until the chicken is fully cooked and the rice breaks down.
Blend or mash with a fork depending on the baby’s age; stir in the olive oil.
The chicken must have no pink parts inside.
Don’t use salt or stock cubes.
Baked carrot and courgette sticks
A pinch of cumin (optional)
Peel the carrot and courgette and cut into finger-thick sticks that fit in the baby’s fist.
Toss with the olive oil and optional cumin.
Space out on the tray and bake for 20–25 minutes until soft enough to squash easily between your fingers.
Once lukewarm, serve so the baby can hold and feed themselves.
Finger foods must be soft enough to squash easily between thumb and forefinger.
Always sit your baby upright and stay with them while they eat.
Vegetable omelette (baby)
1 tablespoon breast milk or water
Squeeze the excess water from the courgette.
Whisk the egg with the milk or water and add the spinach and courgette.
Melt the butter in a small non-stick pan over low heat and pour in the mixture.
Cook covered for 5–6 minutes in total, both sides, until the egg is fully cooked.
Once lukewarm, cut into finger-thick strips and serve.
For babies the egg must be fully cooked with no runny parts.
Egg is an allergenic food; offer it for the first time in the morning and watch the following hours.
Salmon and potato patties
80 g boneless salmon
Boil and mash the potato.
Steam the salmon for 10–12 minutes until fully cooked; feel it with your fingers to make sure no bones remain.
Flake the salmon and mix with the potato, dill and egg yolk.
Shape small flat patties and place on a tray lined with baking paper; brush with olive oil.
Bake for 15 minutes until lightly golden.
Always check fish for bones by hand.
Oily fish is recommended 1–2 times a week.
Keeps 24 hours in the fridge; cooked patties can be frozen for 1 month.
Spinach and curd cheese bites
3 tablespoons unsalted curd cheese
2 tablespoons cooked, finely chopped spinach
Squeeze the water out of the spinach well.
Knead the curd cheese, spinach, oats and egg yolk together.
Shape walnut-sized balls and place on the tray.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until cooked through.
Once lukewarm, halve and serve.
Choose unsalted curd cheese; cheeses sold for babies are often salty.
Limit spinach to 1–2 times a week.
Mini banana oat pancakes
Mash the banana with a fork until smooth.
Add the egg, oats and cinnamon, mix and leave for 5 minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan over low heat and grease lightly with butter.
Drop small portions into the pan with a dessertspoon.
Cook each side for 2–3 minutes, until cooked through.
Once lukewarm, serve in a size the baby can hold.
Don’t add sugar or honey.
Keep the heat low so the egg cooks through.
Keeps 24 hours in the fridge; pancakes can be frozen for 1 month.
Lentil and carrot patties
Wash the lentils and cook with the grated carrot in the water for 15 minutes until they break down.
Take off the heat, add the bulgur and leave covered for 15 minutes.
Add the olive oil and cumin and knead.
Shape small patties that fit in the baby’s fist.
Don’t add salt or tomato paste.
Bulgur contains gluten.

Add the fruit and oats and mix.
